views.title: Place an order, then deliver a receipt
views.description: The browser waits for order confirmation while receipt work continues through a broker. Read the calls and replies in causal order; worker delivery can overlap the browser response.
notes: Fictional success scenario. URLs, payloads, status codes, and broker behavior are examples, not verified APIs.
Event numbers are reading order. Events 7 and 8 share a prerequisite and can overlap; their completion order is not guaranteed.
Replies appear after downstream work, with each exchange paired to its request. A 202 reply means acceptance, not delivery.

events.title: Browser submits the selected items
events.description: The user confirms checkout. The browser waits for an order result before displaying confirmation.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: Orders API requests payment authorization
events.description: After input validation, the handler awaits authorization. No order has been persisted yet.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: Payment provider replies with authorization
events.description: The API checks the authorized result before allowing persistence. Authorization alone does not prove settlement.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: Orders API writes the authorized order
events.description: The handler awaits the database operation; persistence failure belongs in a separate recovery scenario.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: The database returns the stored order ID
events.description: The API receives the inserted ID and can prepare order confirmation. Transaction semantics must be verified in the real implementation.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: Orders API publishes receipt work
events.description: The API starts background receipt delivery. It does not wait for the receipt worker to finish; broker acknowledgement behavior is outside this example.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: Orders API returns order confirmation
events.description: The browser receives the confirmed order and updates its UI. Receipt delivery may still be pending.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: The broker delivers the order event
events.description: The worker starts when the event is delivered. This can happen before or after the browser receives confirmation; no dependency on that reply is implied.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: Receipt worker requests an email
events.description: Inside the independent worker branch, this HTTP request is awaited. A background workflow can contain synchronous request/reply interactions.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: Email service acknowledges the message
events.description: The service accepts delivery work. This reply is not evidence that the email has reached the customer.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.

events.title: Worker records acceptance
events.description: The worker continuation records the accepted result. Retry, broker acknowledgement, and eventual delivery policies require separate source evidence.
notes: Fictional example; replace this contract with traced source.
